title: Breach Predictor Events page and User Threat Profile page: filters, columns and detail panels

prose.text: {{events-scope}} The scope of events differs between pages {{divergence:events-scope-wording}}. {{events-default}}
{{events-columns}} {{event-detail}} The Event Detail panel fields and the CSV contents are open {{gap:event-detail-and-csv}}.
{{users-overview}} {{users-list}} {{users-detail}} The User Detail panel fields are open {{gap:event-detail-and-csv}}.

events-scope.statement: The Events page is for filtering and analyzing the allowed events that have affected the organization during a time period.

quotes: You can use the Events page to filter and analyze all the allowed events that have affected your organization during a particular time period.

events-default.statement: By default the Events page shows events for all threat families and all users; a drop-down at the top right filters by time period.

quotes: By default, Breach Predictor shows events for all threat families and all users.
At the top right of the page, you can use the drop-down menu to filter by time period.

events-filters.statement: The Events page can be filtered by threat family, users, time frame and MITRE ATT&CK tactic, and a CSV file with information about each threat event can be downloaded.

quotes: Filter results by threat family.
Filter results by users in your organization.
Change the time frame for the results shown on the page.
Filter the results by MITRE ATT&CK tactic.
Download a CSV file that contains information about each threat event.

events-columns.statement: The Events table columns are Date/Time (GMT), Policy Status (allowed or blocked by policy), User Name, Threat Name, Threat Type, Tactic, URL and Client Ip; columns can be modified.

quotes: Date/Time: The date and time (GMT) of the threat activity.
Policy Status: Whether the event was allowed or blocked by policy.
User Name: The name of the user in your organization affected by the threat event.
Threat Name: The name of the threat family associated with each event.
Threat Type: The type of threat associated with each event.
Tactic: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic associated with each event.
URL: The URL associated with each event.
Client Ip: The IP address for the client that experienced the threat event.
Modify the columns available in the table.

events-chart.statement: The Events allowed over time bar chart shows the threat events Zscaler identified for each day in the selected period; hovering over a day's bar shows that day's total, and handles on the chart ends adjust the events shown.

quotes: The Events allowed over time bar chart shows you a high-level view of the threat events that Zscaler identified for each day during the selected time period.
To see the total number of events on a particular day, hover over the bar for the day.
You can also use the handle on either end of the chart to adjust the events shown on the page.

event-detail.statement: Clicking an event in the Events table opens the Event Detail panel, and the May 01, 2025 release entry says that on the Events page and the Events tab of Findings, clicking an individual event shows which log data identified the threat.

quotes: To see more detailed information about a particular event, click an event in the table to open the Event Detail panel.
On the Events tab on the Findings page and on the Events page, you can click an individual event to see which log data identified the threat.

events-tactics.statement: On the Events page, the By Tactics options update to show the MITRE ATT&CK tactics associated with the selected threat families.

quotes: the By Tactics options update to indicate the MITRE ATT&CK tactics associated with the selected threat families.

users-overview.statement: The User Threat Profile Overview tab shows the number of users affected at each MITRE ATT&CK stage, the number of users at risk in each department, the number affected by each threat type, and the number at risk by region; on each tab, results can be filtered by users and threats.

quotes: View the number of users affected at each stage of the MITRE ATT&CK matrix.
View the number of users at risk in each department.
View the number of users affected by each threat type.
View the number of users at risk by region.
On each tab, you can filter by users and threats.

users-list.statement: The User Threat Profile Users List tab can be filtered by country, threat, threat type and tactic, and lists User, Department, Location, Device/IP Address, Threat, Threat Type and Tactic for each affected user.

quotes: Filter the results by country, threat, threat type, and tactic.
User: The name and email address for each affected user.
Department: The department to which each affected user belongs.
Location: The geographic location of each affected user.
Device/IP Address: The device and IP address where each threat was identified.
Threat: The name of the threat family affecting each user.
Threat Type: The type of threat affecting each user.
Tactic: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic achieved or predicted for each affected user.

users-detail.statement: Clicking a user's name in the Users List table opens the User Detail panel, with detailed information about how and when the threat affected the user.

quotes: You can click the name of any user on the table to open the User Detail panel, which contains detailed information about how and when the threat affected each user.

events-scope-wording.summary: The Events article describes the Events page as covering allowed events, the Policy Status column shows events allowed or blocked by policy, and the navigation page says the page shows all tracked events.

positions.says: The Events page filters and analyzes all the allowed events.

quotes: You can use the Events page to filter and analyze all the allowed events that have affected your organization during a particular time period.

positions.says: The Policy Status column records whether an event was allowed or blocked by policy.

quotes: Policy Status: Whether the event was allowed or blocked by policy.

positions.says: The Events page provides a view across time of all tracked events.

quotes: The Events page provides a view across time of all tracked events in your organization.

events-scope-wording.impact: Do not state that the Events page lists only allowed events, or that it lists blocked ones, as settled.

event-detail-and-csv.title: Which fields the Event Detail and User Detail panels show, and what the Events CSV export contains
event-detail-and-csv.detail: The Events article ends by introducing a list of Event Detail panel fields that is absent from the capture; the User Detail panel fields are described only as how and when the threat affected the user; the CSV export lists no columns, row limit or time range.
